Oeta – 1956

Victor Vasarely’s screenprint after a 1956 composition: a black and white grid of squares that shears and twists, between large black and white rhombs on a grey ground.

Source
V&A: Print “Oeta – 1956”, CIRC.682-1965
Creator
Victor Vasarely
Made
1959 (print, after a 1956 composition)
Style
Op art (agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Precise, shifting, architectural
Evidence
Downloaded and inspected the V&A image of its copy, CIRC.682-1965 (1267 × 1600 px), with a colour bar at the side, in a scratchpad. No image is stored.
Reviewed
28 September 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

The V&A describes a colour screenprint on paper, 55.5 × 36.8 cm, made in France in 1959, acquired in 1965. V&A.

The V&A calls Vasarely (1908–1997) one of the leading artists of the movement later named Op art, whose aim was to make a static surface seem to move, and notes his use of cheap screenprinting for multiples. V&A.

Observed

  • A mid-grey rectangle sits on a white sheet. On it, a wide band holds a grid of black squares on white.
  • In parts of the grid the squares rotate or shear into rhombs, so the band seems to fold and ripple.
  • Large black squares and black-and-white rhombs, tilted at different angles, sit above and below the grid.
  • Only black, white, and one grey appear.

Why it belongs

Oeta shows the checkerboard as a surface under stress: a few units change shape, and the whole plane seems to bend.

The grey ground is the one step in the value scale that the style record allows.

Borrow

Take a strict grid of black squares and shear a few rows or cells into rhombs to suggest a fold.

Use one mid-grey as a ground to separate a black and white pattern from a white page.
